rationale: Both documents name Raman et al. (2026)'s white-bear steering, built from WorkspaceBench's directed_modulation bench items, as the source, and both frame the new method as using 48 self-authored stance-contrast prompt pairs with no bench items, to test whether the effect generalizes beyond the original bench family. The novelty framing (prompt-source independence of the stance direction in Qwen3.5-4B's mid-depth residual stream) is stated essentially identically in both documents, so there is no material difference in how source, overlap, or novelty are described; the only discrepancy found is the message's inaccurate claim about the write-up file's word count.
